issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter missing @MainActor annotation
issues.description: The rule requires that classes interacting with UIKit or performing UI updates must be marked with @MainActor annotation. The SettingsTextFormatter class formats text for UI display in settings screens but lacks the @MainActor annotation.
issues.rule_name: UI-Related Code Must Be Annotated with @MainActor

issues.title: Incorrect localized string reference in SettingsTextFormatter
issues.description: The formatStudiesText method references strings.detailTextStudies instead of strings.detailTextStudiesV2. This causes the formatter to display the old v1 Studies message ('%@ may install and run studies from time to time.') instead of the new v148 message ('%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.') that was added in this PR. The helper class was clearly intended to format the new v148 strings based on the PR context, but uses the wrong string constant.

issues.title: Inconsistent format specifier documentation in RolloutsSettingMessage comment
issues.description: The comment for RolloutsSettingMessage incorrectly documents the format specifier as '%1$@' (positional format) while the actual value string uses '%@' (simple format). This mismatch creates confusion for localization teams and could lead to incorrect translations, as translators may attempt to use positional formatting based on the comment when the string implementation doesn't support it. The comment should match the actual format specifier used in the value field.

issues.title: Linter exclusion points to wrong message key version
issues.description: The linter configuration exclusion was updated to reference 'Settings.Studies.Message.v148' but the original PR added this key to exclude quotes validation for the v136 message. Since the PR adds new v148 strings with similar content containing quotes, the exclusion should have remained as v136 to maintain the existing exclusion, or both versions should be excluded. This change will cause the linter to fail validation on the v136 string that legitimately needs the exclusion, while potentially missing issues in the new v148 string.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter class missing final keyword
issues.description: The newly added SettingsTextFormatter class violates repository Rule #12 from AGENTS.md, which requires classes that are not designed for subclassing to be marked with the 'final' keyword. This helper class is clearly not intended for inheritance (it has a private initializer and is a simple utility class), but lacks the final modifier. This prevents compiler optimizations and fails to communicate design intent explicitly, violating an explicit compliance rule added in this same PR.

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter and its methods lack explicit access control
issues.description: Rule requires explicit access control modifiers. The new nested class and its members use default (implicit) access levels (`class`, `static let shared`, and `func` declarations have no explicit `internal`/`private`/`public`).
issues.rule_name: Properties and Methods Must Have Appropriate Access Control

issues.title: SettingsTextFormatter should be marked final
issues.description: The helper singleton class is not designed for inheritance but is declared as a non-final class. Per the rule, such classes must be marked `final` to prevent unintended subclassing and enable compiler optimizations.
issues.rule_name: Classes That Should Not Be Subclassed Must Be Marked Final

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #31198 - EXP-5874 Add strings for Rollouts toggle and update Studies strings
pr.author: Bastian Gruber

structured_output.summary:
This PR lands the v148 copy needed to split the Studies toggle into separate Studies and Rollouts toggles: six new keys in `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift` (title/link/message for each feature), mirrored en-CA/en-GB `Settings.strings` entries, matching Focus constants in `UIConstants.swift`, a small `SettingsTextFormatter` helper, and one l10n linter exclusion. No UI is wired up yet — that work lands in #30988, so this is effectively a copy-and-config PR.

The string values themselves are fine, but two defects should be fixed before merge: the Rollouts translator comment cites `%1$@` while the string uses `%@`, which makes the reference-string linter fail, and `SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText` formats the superseded v136 Studies message instead of the new v148 one. The linter exclusion is also unnecessary and should be removed.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The `%1$@`/`%@` comment mismatch will fail the required Firefox reference-string linter CI job, and the new formatter points at the old Studies copy, defeating the purpose of adding the v148 strings. Both are small, targeted fixes.

architecture.overview: Firefox iOS keeps user-facing copy as `MZLocalizedString` declarations in `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`, which wrap `NSLocalizedString` with key/table/value/comment metadata and serve as the source for the en-US XLIFF export that the l10n pipeline consumes. The app currently reads the v136 Studies strings from `AppSettingsTableViewController`, while Focus has an independent copy in `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` read by `SettingsViewController`. This PR adds new v148 Studies and Rollouts keys (and matching Focus constants) without switching any call sites, and adds a helper that will format the new Focus copy once the toggle split in #30988 lands. CI additionally exports the Firefox declarations to XLIFF and runs `moz-xliff-lint` against `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json` for typography, placeables, ellipsis, and hard-coded brand names.
steps: Start at the l10n source of truth: `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`, where each string is declared with a versioned key, table, English value, and translator comment.

This PR appends six `v148` keys — `Settings.Studies.{Title,Link,Message}.v148` and `Settings.Rollouts.{Title,Link,Message}.v148` — while leaving the `v136` keys in place so existing call sites keep working.

The en-CA and en-GB `Settings.strings` tables are updated with the same six keys so those shipped locales have values immediately; all other locales continue to fall back to en-US until the l10n import runs.

For Focus, `UIConstants.strings` gains `labelStudiesV2`, `detailTextStudiesV2`, `labelRollouts`, `detailTextRollouts`, and `detailTextSendUsageDataV2`; `SettingsViewController.initializeToggles()` still reads the v1 constants, so behavior is unchanged.
The PR also adds `SettingsTextFormatter`, an unreferenced wrapper around `String(format:)` intended to render the new Study/Rollout descriptions once #30988 wires the split toggles.
In CI, the Firefox reference-string workflow exports these declarations to `firefox-ios.xliff` and lints it using the `quotes`/`placeables` configuration changed in this PR.

findings.title: Rollouts comment uses `%1$@` but the string uses `%@`, breaking the l10n placeables check
findings.fixPrompt: In `firefox-ios/Shared/Strings.swift`, the comment for `RolloutsSettingMessage` (line 6261) says `%1$@ is the app name` while the value on line 6260 uses `%@`. The moz-xliff-lint placeables check requires the comment to contain the exact placeable token from the value, so the `Firefox: reference string linter` CI job will fail. Change the comment to reference `%@`, matching the value and the sibling `StudiesSettingMessageV3` comment. Do not change the value.

findings.title: SettingsTextFormatter formats the superseded v136 Studies string
findings.fixPrompt: In `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift`, `SettingsTextFormatter.formatStudiesText(appName:)` (line 424) formats `strings.detailTextStudies`, the v136 copy, instead of `strings.detailTextStudiesV2` added at line 207. This makes the new helper render the old Studies description when it is wired up in the toggle split (#30988). Change the helper to format `detailTextStudiesV2`; leave `formatRolloutsText` unchanged.

findings.title: Quotes linter exclusion targets a string with no quote violations
findings.body:
The `quotes` exclusion now points at `Settings.Studies.Message.v148`:

::diff{file=".github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json" lines="6-11"}

The value is `%@ randomly selects users to test features, which improves quality for everyone.` It contains neither a straight `'` nor `"` — the only two characters `check_quotes` looks for — so this exclusion suppresses nothing while silently weakening the check for a brand-new user-facing string. `.github/l10n/README.md` says the only expected exception is hard-coded brand names, and that new exceptions need Localization sign-off.

If the intent was to keep an exception for the legacy message, note that `Settings.Studies.Message.v136` uses a typographic apostrophe (`they’re`) and doesn't need one either. Best to drop the exclusion entirely.
findings.fixPrompt: In `.github/l10n/linter_config_ios.json` line 9, the `quotes` exclusion lists `firefox-ios.xliff:Settings.Studies.Message.v148`, but that string contains no straight single or double quotes, so the exclusion does nothing and weakens the check for a new user-facing string. Remove the exclusion. If CI actually failed on a string, use the ID from the linter log instead. Follow `.github/l10n/README.md`, which reserves exceptions for hard-coded brand names and requires l10n sign-off.

findings.title: New SettingsTextFormatter has no test coverage
findings.body:
`SettingsTextFormatter` is new logic with no test, and the stale-string bug above is exactly what a one-line assertion would catch. `focus-ios/focus-ios-tests/ClientTests` already exercises `UIConstants.strings` keys (for example `BrowserViewControllerTests`), so a small test fits the existing setup: call `formatStudiesText(appName: "Firefox Focus")` and assert the result contains "randomly selects users", then do the same for `formatRolloutsText` with "improve features, performance, and stability".

::diff{file="focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift" lines="417-430"}
findings.fixPrompt: Add a unit test for the new `SettingsTextFormatter` defined in `focus-ios/Blockzilla/UIComponents/UIConstants.swift` (lines 417-430). Put it under `focus-ios/focus-ios-tests/ClientTests`. Assert that `formatStudiesText(appName: "Firefox Focus")` returns the v148 Studies copy containing "randomly selects users" and that `formatRolloutsText` returns the Rollouts copy containing "improve features, performance, and stability". This guards against the helper pointing at the old constant.
